 Order

The petitioner is the accused in S.C.No.155/2023 on the files of the Additional District and Sessions Court (Violence against Women & Children), Ernakulam, which arose out of Crime No.1783/2021 of Maradu Police Station, Ernakulam.

entities.text: Additional District and Sessions Court (Violence against Women & Children), Ernakulam
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
The offences alleged against him are under Sections 341, 323,
415, 376(2)(n), 313 & 506 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860.
The prosecution case is that the petitioner indulged in continuous rape upon the de facto complainant from 28.06.2018 onwards, by giving the false promise of marriage to her.
It is alleged that the petitioner caused miscarriage of pregnancy of the de facto complainant and resorted to physical violence upon her.

Another allegation is that the petitioner resorted to a farce ceremony of marriage with the de facto complainant, and thereafter,
refused to get the above marriage registered.
2. In the present petition, the petitioner would contend that he is totally innocent, and that he has been falsely implicated in this case.

It is further stated that the issue has been amicably settled with the de facto complainant/second respondent, who has filed an affidavit stating that she has no objection in quashing the criminal prosecution proceedings against the petitioner.
Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner, the learned counsel for the second respondent and the learned Public Prosecutor representing the State of Kerala.

5. The facts and circumstances of the case, as revealed from the prosecution records, would clearly show that the sexual relationship between the petitioner and the de facto complainant was consensual.
It is true that there is an allegation raised by the de facto complainant that her consent was obtained by the petitioner, upon the false inducement that he would marry her.

However, the above grievance of the de facto complainant about the breach of promise on the part of the petitioner in marrying her is not subsisting at present, since it is seen from the affidavit filed by the de facto complainant that she has settled the issues with the petitioner.
So also, it is stated that she happened to prefer the complaint due to the peculiar situation during that time, when she was overwhelmed by emotional imbalance.

6. The above facts and circumstances of this case would make it clear that there is absolutely no element of misconception which had vitiated the consent extended by the de facto complainant for having sexual relationship with the petitioner.
Therefore, the offence of rape is prima facie not attracted in the facts and circumstances of the case.
Needless to say that the request of the petitioner to quash the proceedings against him, has to be allowed.
In the result, the petition stands allowed.

The proceedings against the petitioner (accused) in S.C.No.155/2023 on the files of the Additional District and Sessions Court (Violence against Women & Children), Ernakulam, which arose out of Crime No.1783/2021 of Maradu Police Station,
Muhammed Shoukath vs State Of Kerala on 10 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/131151791/
2 Ernakulam, are hereby quashed.
